findings.summary: Clean designed evaluation sweep, ZERO recovery actions triggered: at 18:01:11–15Z — graph-loop/intel-loop/product-loop/runtime-loop/cto-council all had ACTIVE runs ('watchdog does not interrupt potentially valid work'); physics-loop latest completed = 32866107906 success (matches accepted memory); product-beta-repair.yml and frontier-research.yml reported 'no completed run to inspect' (frontier-research.yml had existed only since commit 6afbfa0, 17:45:54Z, with zero completed lifetime runs at this timestamp — extends watchdog #75's 17:51Z observation by 10 minutes; first frontier teams ran later). All three recovery branches (runner-shutdown regex / SPIDER_TRANSIENT_OX_EXHAUSTED / OpenCode+transient-network regex) correctly never fired.

WATCHDOG SELF-SUPERSESSION OF A JUST-COMPLETED SWEEP: every step succeeded and the sweep finished at 18:01:15.4Z, but successor run #78 (32881313083), created 18:01:16Z via workflow_run trigger into the same cancel-in-progress:true group spider-ox-watchdog, caused this run to be stamped cancelled at ~18:01:17Z AFTER its work was done. The design therefore discarded a just-finished evaluation and re-executed an identical sweep ~10s later on a different runner — guaranteed duplicate work whenever a lane completion lands within seconds of a cron tick. Distinct from prior findings about queue-occupancy cancellations: here REAL completed work was thrown away post-hoc.
